tickets.title: Model: collections, tier-clean rule, tidy-all win condition (pure)
tickets.owns: Collection semantics in the pure model, implementing the tier-clean rule (D2 as revised by review decision Q1 = C-1(a), 2026-11-15). A collection is COMPLETE iff its four same-color books are grouped together on ONE tier of the bookshelf — any of the four tiers; tiers interchangeable — AND nothing unrelated shares that tier (the tier holds exactly those four books). TIERS ARE EVALUATED INDEPENDENTLY: what rests on other tiers has no effect. Up to three collections can be complete at the same time. Mixed tiers are physically accepted everywhere with zero feedback (no rejection, warning, hint, or celebration). Completion is recomputed only on committed changes (drop or committed restore), never on pickup or mid-drag (decision Q2); an exact put-back or cancel-restore produces NO incomplete→complete transition, so it never re-fires the celebration; a committed move that breaks a collection quietly stops counting it; a genuine re-group reports the transition again, once. Whole level completes only when every item sits on a valid non-floor placement (slot or surface — not floor, not held; a mat rest counts as floor and does not satisfy tidy-all, C-22) AND all three collections are complete at the same time (tidy-all, D3).
contracts: collectionStatus(): Array<{ id; label; colorKey; complete: boolean; tierId?: string }> — the ONLY way anyone learns collection state; the drag/preview path must not call it; tierId names the completed tier (animation anchor for CC-008)

Cleanliness predicate (per tier, evaluated independently): the collection's four books all rest on one tier T and every item on T belongs to that collection. No per-shelf condition exists — other tiers are never read
Books of different colors may share a tier physically (accepted, never complete) — accepts all four physically but gives no correctness feedback
Anti-spam guarantee is model-side (Q2): status recomputed only on committed changes; exact put-backs (same location kind + coordinates) and cancel-restores never produce a collectionCompleted entry

Completed boolean on DropResult is the level-complete transition; new optional field collectionCompleted?: string[] lists collections that just transitioned incomplete→complete on this committed change
Evaluation happens on committed changes only (never during drag)
isComplete(): all items on valid NON-FLOOR placements AND all three collections complete at the same time — total comes from level data
acceptance: 3 green + 1 red on one tier: drop accepted, no completion reported, no feedback
4 green grouped on a tier + unrelated item on THAT SAME tier: green NOT complete
4 green grouped on a tier + unrelated item on ANOTHER tier: green IS complete (tiers independent)
Same grouping on any of the four tiers: complete (tiers interchangeable)
Two collections simultaneously (tier 1 + tier 2): both complete
Three simultaneously (winning arrangement, plan §8.4: 4 red t1 + 4 green t2 + 4 blue t3 + 16 non-books in home slots): level complete under tidy-all
Removing one book from a complete collection: status silently false, no event
Re-grouping afterwards: completes again (reports the transition once)
Pick up a book from a complete tier and put it straight back: status stays complete; collectionCompleted stays empty (no re-celebration)
Cancel-restore of a member: same — no transition, no re-celebration
Book left on the counter blocks level completion under tidy-all; a mat rest also does not (walkable floor)

tickets.title: Seeded scatter + Reset (same layout) / New Mess (new layout)
tickets.owns: Replayable, deterministic layouts. Pure scatter module with mulberry32 PRNG; rejection-sampled placement over walkable floor space (room bounds minus wall margin minus furniture footprints; footprint-aware spacing — AABBs non-overlapping + ≥ 0.2 gap, the ≥ 0.7 shorthand center-to-center for the small-item class mugs/books/shoes/towels; ≥ 0.5 from furniture; rotation ±21°) with a documented fallback chain (relaxed spacing → grid → shipped default layout) that always terminates in a valid layout; Reset re-scatters with the SAME seed; New Mess draws a fresh seed and re-scatters; ?seed= pins layouts for tests (untrusted input: finite integer → uint32 clamp → default seed on invalid, C-19); validation helpers with pinned signatures exported for tests — the solver generates and checks moves ONLY through the model's own predicates (validateSurfaceDrop, slot rules, tier-clean rule), slots-only search space (32 ≥ 28; the winning arrangement §8.4 uses only slots), declared step budget with a distinct budget-exceeded failure reason, reachability operationalized as start cell (0.15 grid) outside every footprint; solver consumes static-decor-adjusted effective bounds (C-7); HUD buttons wired; Play again = New Mess.
contracts: scatter(seed, level): { x, y, rotation }[] — deterministic; same seed ⇒ identical layout
Safety: every start point inside walkable floor area, AABBs non-overlapping + ≥ 0.2 gap (the ≥ 0.7 shorthand is center-to-center for small items), ≥ 0.5 from furniture AABBs, rotation within ±21°

Reachability, operationalized (C-12): isLayoutReachable(level, positions, cell = 0.15): boolean — start cell outside every footprint (items + furniture); no free-space path search (drags fly over furniture)

Arrangement check (C-12): hasValidArrangement(level, positions): { ok: boolean; reason?: 'no-arrangement' | 'budget-exceeded' } — slots-only backtracking solver driven ONLY by the model's own predicates (validateSurfaceDrop, slot rules, tier-clean rule); declared step budget; exceedance reports budget-exceeded, never a silent pass; consumes static-decor-adjusted effective bounds
Model API: reset(seed?) — no seed reuses current seed; newMess(): draws fresh seed (stored on the instance); ?seed= untrusted input: finite integer → uint32 clamp → default seed on invalid (C-19)
acceptance: Reset twice in a row → pixel-identical scatter after settle
New Mess twice → different layouts (overwhelming probability; asserted as 'at least one differing position')
Generated layouts pass spacing, reachability and arrangement checks for ≥ 100 sampled seeds in tests
Buttons work with pointer + keyboard; completion card resets state cleanly
An artificially tiny budget reports budget-exceeded (named test)
The winning arrangement (§8.4) passes hasValidArrangement and completes the level through the public model API
Invalid ?seed= values (non-numeric, float, out-of-range) fall back to the default seed
tickets.completionNote: scatter.ts (mulberry32, rejection sampling with stepwise-relaxed spacing, jittered-grid fallback, shipped default), validators (isLayoutReachable cell-based, hasValidArrangement slots-only via model predicates with budget-exceeded, isScatterSafe), model reset(seed?)/newMess()/currentSeed, ?seed= via pure parseSeedParam. Two sampler bugs found and fixed during the 100-seed sweep (furniture-clearance clause, self-overlap exclusion). 75 tests green.

tickets.title: HUD & completion presentation — collection chips, tidy-all gating
tickets.owns: The HUD and end-of-level presentation: three collection chips (colored dots, filled = currently complete, quiet on break), progress placed/total where 'placed' = items on NON-FLOOR valid placements (slot or surface; floor rests do not count — C-21), completion card gated by the tidy-all rule, updated hint copy, seed shown subtly for reproducibility.
contracts: Chips render from collectionStatus() on committed changes only (no drag-time correctness info)
placed = count of items with location.kind ∈ {slot, surface} (non-floor); total = level.items.length (28); HUD count and card gate must agree (named HUD-vs-card consistency test)
Completion card ('Home, at last.') only on the model's completed transition; Play again → New Mess

Chips recompute from collectionStatus() on committed changes only (Q2): pickup does not recompute; exact put-backs and cancel-restores produce no transition; a held member does not change the chip until the drop commits
acceptance: Chip fills/stays filled exactly when its collection is currently complete; breaking quietly un-fills; a held member does not change the chip until the drop commits
Card never appears while any item rests on the floor even if all collections are complete
No new correctness hints introduced anywhere in the HUD
HUD count and card gate agree in every tested state (named test)
tickets.verify: manual walkthrough + Playwright assertions in CC-016
tickets.completionNote: Collection chips (filled = currently complete, quiet un-fill), tidy-all progress semantics via model, New Mess button + Play again = New Mess, seed shown as title on the HUD sub, intro hint copy. HUD-vs-card consistency named test added.

contracts: Real pointer events only + read-only __cozy hook (incl. the lastSfx log and the itemClientPos surface branch); ?seed= pins layouts where determinism is asserted
